claims.text: The target component is made from a FeCoNiCrMo0.2-based alloy and has localized surface damage, microcracks, and degraded wear and corrosion resistance.
The proposed intervention is laser cladding of a FeCoNiCrMo0.2-based composite coating containing 32% WC and 2% nano-CeO2 under an inert atmosphere.
The proposed laser-cladding treatment will produce a dense coating microstructure.
The proposed laser-cladding treatment will produce a fine-grained coating microstructure.
WC and nano-CeO2 will be uniformly dispersed and reinforce the coating matrix.
The WC and nano-CeO2 additions will create a passivated surface layer.
Rapid melting and solidification during laser cladding will minimize the heat-affected zone.
Minimizing the heat-affected zone will prevent thermal gradients associated with hot cracking.
Thermal gradients are a cause of hot cracking in the specified repair system.
WC and nano-CeO2 additions promote grain refinement in the FeCoNiCrMo0.2-based coating.
WC and nano-CeO2 additions suppress defects in the coating.
Grain refinement and defect suppression caused by the additives enhance wear resistance.
Grain refinement, defect suppression, and surface passivation caused by the additives enhance corrosion resistance.
The laser-clad surface will have significantly higher hardness than traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
The laser-clad surface will have significantly better wear resistance than traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
The laser-clad surface will have significantly better corrosion resistance than traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
The laser-clad surface will exhibit a markedly lower incidence of hot cracking than traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Insufficient thermal control may limit the effectiveness of the intervention.
A substrate that differs significantly from the FeCoNiCrMo0.2-based system may limit the effectiveness of the intervention.
